evidence: src/domain/order/OrderStatus.ts: canTransition(from, to) is the only place transition rules live, using FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE and CANCELLABLE_STATUSES
src/domain/order/Order.ts: private transitionTo calls canTransition(this.currentStatus, target) and does not repeat the rules; pay/pack/ship/deliver/cancel all go through transitionTo
src/domain/order/OrderLine.ts: lineTotal = unitPrice.multiply(quantity.value); Order.total only adds up line.lineTotal using Money.add
src/domain/order/Order.ts: the checks on new orders (customer, non-empty lines, unique productId) appear only in static place()
src/domain/order/OrderRepository.ts: interface with findById/findAll/findByStatus/save, typed with Order and OrderStatus from this module
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All four files deal with one concern, the Order aggregate. Order.ts is the aggregate root. OrderLine.ts is its child value object. OrderStatus.ts holds the status vocabulary and the transition rules. OrderRepository.ts is the persistence port for the aggregate.

Each invariant lives in one place:
- Transition legality is defined only in OrderStatus.ts (canTransition, FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATUSES). Order.transitionTo calls it rather than repeating the rules.
- Line totals are computed only in OrderLine.lineTotal. Order.total adds up those values instead of recomputing them.
- The checks on new orders (customer present, at least one line, no repeated products) appear only in Order.place.

The module's own abstractions are used consistently. Order relies on the shared Money and Quantity value objects. restore/toSnapshot map lines through OrderLine, Quantity.of and Money.ofCents. OrderRepository uses the Order and OrderStatus types.

Order.restore skips the checks in place, but that is the normal way to rebuild an aggregate from storage, not a bypass. FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE repeats part of ORDER_STATUSES, but both are in the same file and describe different things (every possible status vs. the forward path), so the invariant is not split across files.
